Subject: Follow-up: SKU modelling, token targets & trial top-up

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can size the trial/top-up and get procurement moving:

1) Usage profile you mentioned on the call: 5M tokens/month initial (pilot), forecast to 25–35M tokens/month by month 6. Can you confirm the breakouts by route (inference generation vs. embeddings) and any peak TPS windows?

2) Budget band & target unit economics: you said procurement expects to see economic cases with a target cost-of-inference anywhere between $300–$700 per 1M tokens depending on model fidelity. Can you confirm the preferred target (we usually present a conservative and an aggressive band)?

3) Trial/top-up ask: we can approve a one-time credit top-up while procurement completes the PO if the burn pattern looks healthy. To proceed we need:
   - Procurement contact and billing email (so legal/finance can prepare a short order form)
   - Confirmation that test traffic will stay under 5k concurrent requests and that any PII is redacted during the pilot (standard guardrail)

Attached is a short econ template (redwood-econ-template.xlsx) — if you fill the expected monthly token volumes and ratio of generation:embedding we’ll return a tailored $/1M token proposal and a recommended trial credit amount.

Next steps: if you can reply with the procurement contact + the filled template by early next week I’ll route the credit approval to finance (Ben will sign-off on the technical guardrails).

Thanks,
Irene
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers below and I attached a completed econ sheet in-line on the callnotes (we also uploaded to our internal drive).

- Route split: we expect ~80% generation (customer-facing responses) and ~20% embeddings (vector store updates + similarity).
- Monthly volumes: pilot month 1 = 5M tokens, ramp month 3 = 12M, month 6 = 30M.
- Peaks: we see daily peaks ~11–2pm PT; concurrency rarely above 3k except for promos (we’ll notify ahead of runbooks).
- Budget band: procurement is targeting $400–$600 per 1M tokens at our expected fidelity. Lower is better but they need to see an SLA + fallbacks for cost spikes.

Procurement contact: procurement@retaillytics.ai (CCed).

For the trial top-up: we’d like an initial credit of $6,000 to cover the first month overages while PO completes. If you can condition the top-up on the guardrails you mentioned (concurrency cap, no raw PII, and daily burn alerts) we can sign-off quickly.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Olivia

Hi Olivia / Irene —

Following up with a short technical and commercial note so finance has what they need for the approval flow.

Technical guardrails (we recommend these for the trial top-up):
- Concurrency cap: 5k requests (we’ll set a soft throttle at 4.5k to avoid sudden cutovers)
- Prefix caching enabled for repeat flows (reduces effective token spend)
- KV-cache TTL 12 hours for session affinity during A/B tests
- No PII in demo traffic — if any PII must be tested we run on a private Dedicated instance (requires separate review)

Commercial suggestion:
- We can approve an initial trial credit of $6,000 as requested with the following conditions: daily burn alerts to SL (procurement@retaillytics.ai), a usage report at day 7, and an automated top-up trigger requiring a hand-off to procurement for any additional credits above $6k.
- Based on your 30M/month target at steady-state the recommended unit price is $350 per 1M tokens using our quantized zl-2 profile for generation-heavy workloads. That maps to ~$10,500/month at 30M tokens (generation-heavy). We’ll provide a conservative and an aggressive pricing tier in the order form.

I’ve attached the approval stub for finance (trial-credit-approval.md) — Irene, if you’re good with this I’ll route to Ops & Finance for the one-time credit.

Ben Carter
